newsitem.title: CHINA: China says weather made veteran miss Deng funeral.
newsitem.headline: China says weather made veteran miss Deng funeral.

text.p: Beijing's cold weather forced China's most senior surviving revolutionary to miss memorial rites this week for former paramount leader Deng Xiaoping, the parliamentary spokesman said on Friday.

Chinese sources have said Peng Zhen, 95, formerly one of Deng's closest associates and allies, missed the patriarch's memorial service on Tuesday after being hospitalised for severe vomiting early this month.

Zhou Jue, spokesman for the National People's Congress, did not give any details of Peng's health but said chilly weather in the Chinese capital had forced his absence from the nation's funeral of the decade.

"Comrade Peng Zhen is a senior proletarian revolutionary of the elder generation ... the Beijing weather is very cold at the moment and he cannot go outside," Zhou said, adding that Peng's wife and children had gone to Deng's memorial instead.
Chinese sources said Peng was admitted to Beijing Hospital in the city centre during the Lunar New Year holidays, which began on February 7.

Deng died late on February 19 at the age of 92, and Peng's absence from Deng's funeral was a signal he could be seriously ill, since China's five other most senior surviving revolutionary leaders all attended.

They were former president Yang Shangkun, 89, former parliament chief Wan Li, 81, retired Politburo standing committee member Song Ping, 80, former vice-premier Bo Yibo, 90, and retired general Song Renqiong, 92.

Peng is a veteran hardliner who stepped down as chairman of the National People's Congress (NPC) in April 1988 as part of a drive to retire ageing communist comrades, but retained widespread influence.

Mayor of Beijing for 15 years and a close ally of then head of state Liu Shaoqi, Peng was hounded from office in June, 1966, by radicals charging he had transformed Beijing into a personal empire from which to combat Chairman Mao Zedong's policies.
He returned to prominence in the late 1970s along with longtime ally, Deng, and was appointed NPC chairman in 1983, a job that afforded him ample opportunity to build a power base.
